instruction: I've built a Snake game in Python, and the gameplay is solid! However, the game window feels a bit cramped at 600x400 pixels. I'd like to make it larger so there's more room to maneuver. Could you update the window dimensions to 800x600 pixels? This should give a better playing experience with more space. Thanks!

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing window dimensions from 600x400 to 800x600 in settings.py. Evaluator uses AST parsing to check WIDTH and HEIGHT values with partial credit (0.5 per dimension).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct WIDTH, 0.5 for correct HEIGHT

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both width (800) and height (600) requirements from the instruction - complete coverage
AST parsing logic is the correct semantic approach to extract WIDTH and HEIGHT variable assignments from Python source code (python_code.py:44-77)
Metric robustly handles both tuple assignments (WIDTH, HEIGHT = 800, 600) AND separate assignments (WIDTH = 800; HEIGHT = 600)
Partial credit scoring (0.5 per dimension) is semantically appropriate for this two-part requirement
Expected values are semantically correct: width=800, height=600 exactly match the instruction's requirement to update from 600x400 to 800x600
get_vm_file getter correctly fetches all Python files including settings.py where dimensions are defined

Metric function correctly handles expected parameter - when expected.type='rule', it receives rules dict directly and correctly accesses expected.get('width') and expected.get('height') (python_code.py:79-80)
Edge cases properly handled: empty file list returns 0.0 (line 18-19), missing settings.py returns 0.0 (line 36-37), parsing errors return 0.0 (line 90-91)

File path handling is semantically correct: iterates actual_files list (line 28), uses os.path.basename() to find settings.py (line 30), os.path.exists() to verify (line 36), open() to read content (line 41) - static validator warnings are false positives
Runtime feasibility: Logic will work correctly - AST parsing can extract variable assignments from saved Python files, no postconfig needed
Complete semantic verification: Evaluator can definitively verify whether the task was completed correctly by checking the actual WIDTH and HEIGHT values in the modified settings.py source code
